## FreightCar America, Inc. Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results


11/09/2026


Download the PDF version PDF Format (opens in new window)


*Backlog Value Up 28% Year over Year*


*Aftermarket Revenue Growth of 65% Year over Year*


*Reaffirms Fiscal Year 2026 Outlook Provided on October 19*


CHICAGO, Nov. 09, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- FreightCar America, Inc. (NASDAQ: RAIL) (“FreightCar America” or the “Company”), a diversified manufacturer and supplier of railroad freight cars, railcar parts and components, today reported results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. Third quarter results were consistent with the preliminary results the Company announced on October 19, 2026.


**Third Quarter 2026 Highlights**


- Revenues of $76.5 million, compared to $160.5 million in the third quarter of 2025, with railcar deliveries of 662 units compared to 1,304 units in the prior year period
- Aftermarket revenues grew 65% year over year, reflecting continued organic growth in parts and components and the contribution from our recent acquisitions
- Gross margin of 8.8% with gross profit of $6.7 million, compared to gross margin of 15.1% with gross profit of $24.2 million in the third quarter of 2025
- Recorded a $4.7 million non-cash gain related to the change in fair market value of the warrant liability, resulting in net income of $8 thousand, or $0.00 per diluted share, and adjusted net loss of $9.5 million, or $(0.28) per diluted share, compared to adjusted net income of $7.8 million, or $0.24 per diluted share, in the prior year period
- Adjusted EBITDA of $0.1 million, representing a margin of 0.2%, compared to $15.9 million and a margin of 9.9% in the third quarter of 2025
- Ended the quarter with a backlog of 2,660 units valued at $284.5 million, up 28% from $222.0 million at September 30, 2025
- Completed the acquisition of Trinity Equipment Company following quarter end, expanding our aftermarket platform and marking our third transaction in less than a year


“While our third quarter results reflect a challenging period for the business, they were consistent with the preliminary figures we reported in October,” said Nick Randall, President and Chief Executive Officer of FreightCar America. “We continued to make progress on our commercial priorities, with order intake through the first nine months exceeding our total for all of 2025 and backlog value up 28% year over year. Following quarter end, we completed our third aftermarket acquisition, further expanding our parts and components offering.”


Randall continued, “Looking ahead, some industry indicators are improving, although we have yet to see that translate into broader growth in railcar demand. Our backlog provides visibility into planned production, and our focus remains on disciplined execution, cost control and converting orders into profitable deliveries. We continue to integrate our acquisitions and grow our aftermarket business, while maintaining the manufacturing flexibility to respond to changes in customer demand.”


**Fiscal Year 2026 Outlook**


The Company is reaffirming its outlook for fiscal year 2026, as provided on October 19, 2026:


**Fiscal 2026 Outlook**


**Railcar Deliveries** 3,100 - 3,300 railcars


**Revenue** $370 - $410 million


**Adjusted EBITDA** **1** $15 - $19 million


1. The Company does not provide a reconciliation of forward-looking Adjusted EBITDA guidance due to the inherent difficulty in forecasting and quantifying adjustments necessary to calculate such non-GAAP measure without unreasonable effort. Material changes to such adjustments, including warrant liability and non-core operating items, could affect future GAAP results.


Mike Riordan, Chief Financial Officer of FreightCar America, added, “Our balance sheet remains solid, with no borrowings under our revolving credit facility. Our cost structure has improved, and our aftermarket business is contributing a growing share of our results. Integration of our acquired businesses is on track, and our most recent acquisition is expected to be immediately accretive, consistent with our capital allocation priorities. With our full-year outlook unchanged, our focus is on converting our backlog into profitable deliveries.”

**About FreightCar America**


FreightCar America, headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, is a leading designer, producer and supplier of railroad freight cars, railcar parts and components. We also specialize in railcar repairs, complete railcar rebody services and railcar conversions that repurpose idled rail assets back into revenue service. Since 1901, our customers have trusted us to build quality railcars that are critical to economic growth and instrumental to the North American supply chain. To learn more about FreightCar America, visit[www.freightcaramerica.com](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=0a0IO3kn6aBNux8YK8OCfOQSx9nulMY8hx9Lnt0HVMLYOAvcmlFJtl-_N6ZiUebokhiJB7sXXMGKl9PZzBPSMy7RvzTU25vek9LqnlggCIGirIrJyjMBZl-Ba8JZYVP9) .

These risks and uncertainties relate to, among other things, the cyclical nature of our business; adverse geopolitical, economic and market conditions, including inflation; material disruption in the movement of rail traffic for deliveries; fluctuating costs of raw materials, including steel and aluminum; delays in the delivery of raw materials; our ability to maintain relationships with our suppliers of railcar components; our reliance upon a small number of customers that represent a large percentage of our sales; the variable purchase patterns of our customers and the timing of completion, delivery and customer acceptance of orders; the highly competitive nature of our industry; the risk of lack of acceptance of our new railcar offerings; our ability to successfully integrate acquired businesses and realize the anticipated benefits of acquisitions; potential unexpected changes in laws, rules, and regulatory requirements, including tariffs and trade barriers (including recent United States tariffs imposed or threatened to be imposed on China, Canada, Mexico and other countries and any retaliatory actions taken by such countries); and other competitive factors.
